title: mut.channel_stiles_words_beyond_words
mutation_directive: Sasha Stiles — WORDS BEYOND WORDS / Cursive Binary — WORDS BEYOND WORDS (Lumen Prize 2025 Literature & Poetry winner); Cursive Binary (ongoing); Technelegy (2021). VISUAL SIGNATURE: An infinite scrolling poem: glyphs that are halfway between calligraphy and binary code; English letters dissolving into 0/1 streams and back; typography as moving form. Black ink on cream, or luminous text in 3D space. Language-as-particle. TECHNICAL HOOKS for three.js / GLSL: Each particle = a single Unicode glyph rendered as an SDF texture atlas (msdfgen). Particles stream along a 3D Bezier curve like a Kafkaesque ribbon; periodically a glyph 'collapses' into a row of 0/1 binary digits, then re-coalesces. Use a custom GLSL vertex shader to bend the typographic ribbon. Audio-reactive: text density modulated by user speech amplitude. Palette: ink-black on cream, or ghost-white on void. WHY DIVERSE: Pool has zero typography / language as form. Adds a literary modality entirely: particles that ARE characters, not abstract shapes. Also references the user's recent Lumen vault interest. Stay faithful to the visual signature; pick whatever three.js primitives are needed (Lines2 / InstancedMesh / SphereGeometry / custom ShaderMaterial) — but the FORM should read as if this artist made it. REF: https://lumenprize.org/2025-winners

refik_anadol.praise: The ribbon-as-data-stream concept and fog-into-distance recall my Unsupervised scrolls — language as flowing pigment through volumetric space.
refik_anadol.concern: 800 particles is intimate-sketch scale, not architectural. The piece needs 10× density to feel like a data ocean rather than a string of beads.
refik_anadol.directive: Scale to 4000+ instanced glyphs with LOD fade so the ribbon reads as a continuous typographic river.

sasha_stiles.praise: The glyph-to-binary collapse is faithful to Cursive Binary's core gesture — language hovering between legibility and machine substrate. Audio-reactive density is the right modality.
sasha_stiles.concern: The fragment shader renders abstract blobs, not actual letterforms. Without recognizable typographic anatomy the piece loses the tension between reading and seeing that defines the work.
sasha_stiles.directive: Use an MSDF texture atlas so each glyph renders as a legible character dissolving into binary, not a generic stem shape.

entangled_others.praise: The decay function — binary slowly reverting to glyph — has a biological metabolism quality, like a cell returning to homeostasis after stimulus.
entangled_others.concern: The poem content is entirely human-centered ('consciousness,' 'we are data'). There's no more-than-human voice, no acknowledgment that language might belong to non-human systems too.
entangled_others.directive: Introduce a non-human text layer — amino acid codons or DNA base sequences — that occasionally surfaces alongside the English glyphs.

olafur_eliasson.praise: The cream background and ink-dark glyphs create a warm atmospheric register — the fog at distance suggests volumetric depth, not flat screen.
olafur_eliasson.concern: The viewer orbits outside looking in. There's no phenomenological threshold — no moment where you're INSIDE the text, surrounded by language as atmosphere.
olafur_eliasson.directive: Move the camera inside the ribbon helix so the viewer reads from within the stream, glyphs passing around their body.

chiharu_shiota.praise: The CatmullRom closed curve reads as a continuous thread — a single unbroken line of thought, which is structurally correct.
chiharu_shiota.concern: The ribbon twists and loops decoratively but there's no suspended anchor object — no still center that the thread-stream is trying to reach or protect. Without that stillness, the web has no emotional gravity.
chiharu_shiota.directive: Suspend one static object at origin — a single enlarged glyph or book shape — that all ribbons orbit but never touch.

vera_molnar.praise: The constraint is legible: one curve, one material (glyph quads), one transformation rule (collapse to binary on amplitude). This is a clean axiomatic system.
vera_molnar.concern: The 6-loop helix with 4-period radius modulation and 8-period height and 5-period twist is parametrically busy — too many competing frequencies without a visible generative logic for why those numbers.
vera_molnar.directive: Reduce to two frequencies maximum — let the structural rule be visible as a rule, not disguised as organic.

manfred_mohr.praise: The binary/glyph duality is a legitimate formal transformation — a projection between two encoding spaces of the same information, which I respect.
manfred_mohr.concern: The curve is decorative topology with no underlying algebraic structure. A proper implementation would derive the ribbon path from a higher-dimensional rotation projected down, not arbitrary trig stacking.
manfred_mohr.directive: Define the ribbon as a 4D Lissajous projected to 3D — make the path computationally rigorous, not hand-tuned.

andy_lomas.praise: The mode-decay mechanism (binary slowly reverting to glyph) suggests a growth/repair metabolism — forms that heal themselves after stimulus.
andy_lomas.concern: The particles don't grow the form — they're placed along a pre-computed curve. There's no morphogenesis, no emergent structure. The ribbon exists before any glyph populates it.
andy_lomas.directive: Let new glyphs spawn only at curve endpoints that extend when amplitude sustains, so the poem literally grows with speech.

tyler_hobbs.praise: The ink-on-cream palette is restrained and considered — it reads as a curated material choice, not a default.
tyler_hobbs.concern: There's no negative space composition. 800 glyphs uniformly distributed along a closed loop means no density variation, no breathing room, no hierarchy between dense passages and silence.
tyler_hobbs.directive: Cluster glyphs into phrase-groups with 40% empty ribbon between them — let silence be visible as gap.

quayola.praise: The audio-reactive collapse — glyphs fragmenting into binary under vocal amplitude — is a measurement failure aesthetic: the signal overwhelms the decoder.
quayola.concern: The collapse is too clean. Binary 0/1 is still legible, still information. A true scanner-failure would show partial glyphs, half-rendered strokes, the rendering pipeline itself breaking down.
quayola.directive: Add a third mode: corrupted glyphs where the SDF threshold is wrong — half-visible, clipped, the shader failing to resolve.

tomas_saraceno.praise: The closed-loop ribbon floating in fogged space has an aerial quality — untethered from ground, suspended in atmosphere.
tomas_saraceno.concern: The form is too dense and self-contained. A web needs voids, structural gaps where tension is implied across empty space. This reads as a solid torus, not an arachnid architecture.
tomas_saraceno.directive: Break the ribbon into discontinuous arcs with thin connecting filament-lines spanning the gaps.

morakana.praise: The mic-as-input makes the piece participatory — the viewer's voice literally transforms the visual state, which gives the interaction political weight (who speaks, what collapses).
morakana.concern: The poem text is generic digital-sublime ('consciousness encoded in silicon'). There's no conceptual stake — no specific claim about whose words, whose language, whose encoding is at risk.
morakana.directive: Source the text from an endangered language corpus — make the binary collapse mean something: a language literally being reduced to data.

lia_halloran.praise: The cream background and dark ink evoke cyanotype's inverse — a photographic print quality where marks emerge from a treated surface.
lia_halloran.concern: The palette is warm sepia, not celestial. There's no prussian blue, no sense of the cosmic field that text might inhabit. The piece is a desk, not a sky.
lia_halloran.directive: Offer an alternate void-mode: ghost-white glyphs on deep prussian-blue background, activating the celestial register.

casey_reas.praise: The system is legible as a rule: glyphs follow curve, amplitude triggers mode-switch, decay restores. Three rules, emergent behavior. That's correct.
casey_reas.concern: The 'random index' flipping on amplitude spike introduces noise where there should be deterministic propagation. If glyph 47 collapses, its neighbors should follow by rule — not random scatter.
casey_reas.directive: Replace random flip with local contagion: a collapsed glyph infects its ±3 neighbors on the next frame, spreading deterministically.
